input: How many days of annual leave does a full-time employee with less than 3 years' service receive?
expected_output: A full-time employee with less than 3 years' continuous service receives 27 days of annual leave plus the 8 England and Wales bank holidays, a total of 35 paid days off per leave year (262.5 hours).
context: Less than 3 years | 27 | 8 | 35
Less than 3 years | 27 | 8 | 35 | 262.5
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.1 Annual leave entitlement

**Table 6.1 — Annual leave entitlement for full-time employees (37.5 hours per week, 5 days per week)**

|**Continuous service completed**|**Annual leave (days)**|**Bank holidays (days)**|**Total paid days off per leave**|
|---|---|---|---|
||||**year**|
|Less than 3 years|27|8|35|
|3 years or more, but less than 5 years|28|8|36|
|5 years or more|29|8|37|

- One day of annual leave equals **7.5 hours** for a full-time employee.

- The service-related increase applies from the **first 1 January that falls after** the date on which the employee completes the required continuous service. It is not applied part-way through a leave year.

- The entitlement applies to permanent and fixed-term employees, apprentices and interns. Part-time employees receive a pro-rated entitlement calculated in hours (section 6.3).

- Contractors and agency workers do not receive Northstar annual leave; agency workers' holiday is provided through their agency.

### **Statutory minimum holiday**

Almost all workers are legally entitled to 5.6 weeks' paid holiday per year, capped at 28 days for someone working 5 or more days a week. Employers may include bank holidays within the 5.6 weeks. Northstar's entitlement of 27 days plus 8 bank holidays (35 days for a full-time employee) exceeds the statutory minimum. No pro-rating or rounding rule in this handbook will ever reduce an employee's entitlement below the statutory minimum.

input: What is the deadline for reporting sickness absence on the first day?
expected_output: Employees must call their line manager by telephone or Teams call no later than 09:30 on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least 1 hour before their shift or rota period starts. The absence must also be recorded in PeopleHub the same day.
context: Call your line manager (telephone or Teams voice/video call) no later than 09:30 on the first day of absence.
By 09:30 on the first day of absence; shift and on-call workers at least 1 hour before the shift or rota period.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.1 Reporting an absence

### **How to report sickness**

1. **Call** your line manager (telephone or Teams voice/video call) no later than **09:30** on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least **1 hour before** their shift or rota period starts. 2. If your line manager is unavailable, call your Head of Department or team lead. Leaving a voicemail is acceptable only if you also send a message and follow up with a call before 12:00. 3. Text messages, emails or chat messages alone are not sufficient, except where you are physically unable to speak; in that case, send a message and call as soon as you are able. 4. Record the absence in PeopleHub on the same day, or ask your manager to do so on your behalf. 5. Tell your manager the reason for absence in general terms, your expected return date, and any work that needs urgent cover. You do not have to disclose a diagnosis.

input: What is the deadline for submitting an expense claim?
expected_output: Expense claims must be submitted in ExpenseFlow within 30 calendar days of the date the expense was incurred. Claims 31 to 90 days late need a written explanation and Head of Department approval; claims more than 90 days late are not reimbursed without a Finance Director exception.
context: Submit claims in ExpenseFlow within 30 calendar days of the date the expense was incurred.
Submit within 30 calendar days of the date the expense was incurred.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
12 Expenses and business travel > 12.3 Claim deadline and late claims

## **Expense claim deadline**

Submit claims in ExpenseFlow within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted 31 to 90 calendar days after the expense require a written explanation and Head of Department approval. Claims submitted more than 90 calendar days after the expense are not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the employee was on long-term sickness absence). Leavers must submit all claims within **10 working days** after their leaving date.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Submission deadlines

### **Deadlines**

- Submit within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. For multi-day trips, each expense's own date applies, but all expenses for one trip should be submitted together within 30 calendar days of the first expense of the trip.

- **31 to 90 calendar days:** a late claim requires a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- **More than 90 calendar days:** not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the claimant was on long-term sickness or family leave).

- **Leavers:** all claims must be submitted within **10 working days** after the leaving date. Claims received after that are not paid.

The extension must be confirmed in writing before the original probation end date; probation is not automatically passed or failed if no outcome is issued.

input: What are Northstar's standard working hours and core hours?
expected_output: The standard full-time week is 37.5 hours, worked Monday to Friday as 7.5 hours per day excluding a 60-minute unpaid lunch. The standard day is 09:00 to 17:30, but employees may vary start and finish times within the flexible band of 07:30 to 19:00 provided they are available during core hours of 10:00 to 16:00.
context: The standard full-time working week is 37.5 hours, worked Monday to Friday as 7.5 hours per day excluding an unpaid lunch break of 60 minutes.
provided they are available during the core hours of 10:00 to 16:00
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
5 Working hours, attendance and time recording > 5.1 Standard working week

The standard full-time working week is **37.5 hours** , worked Monday to Friday as **7.5 hours per day** excluding an unpaid lunch break of 60 minutes. The standard day is 09:00 to 17:30, but employees may vary their start and finish times within the flexible band of **07:30 to 19:00** , provided they are available during the core hours of **10:00 to 16:00** and their team's coverage arrangements are met.

Part-time employees work the hours and days set out in their contract. Their core-hours expectation applies only on their contracted working days and only for the hours they are contracted to work.

input: How quickly must I report a lost or stolen company laptop?
expected_output: Report loss or theft of any device to the IT Service Desk immediately and in any case within 1 hour of discovery so it can be locked and wiped remotely. Theft must also be reported to the police within 24 hours, with the crime reference recorded in the IT ticket. Loss or theft is also a security incident.
context: Report loss or theft of any device or access card to the IT Service Desk immediately and in any case within 1 hour of discovery
Report theft to the police within 24 hours and record the crime reference number in the IT ticket.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
20 Company equipment and property > 20.3 Damage, loss and theft

- Report loss or theft of any device or access card to the IT Service Desk **immediately and in any case within 1 hour** of discovery, so that it can be locked and wiped remotely. Loss or theft is also a security incident (section 19.10).

- Report theft to the police within **24 hours** and record the crime reference number in the IT ticket.

- Report accidental damage to the IT Service Desk as soon as possible. Northstar does not normally recover the cost of accidental damage. Where loss or damage results from deliberate misuse or gross negligence, Northstar may recover a reasonable contribution only with the employee's written agreement or where the contract permits.

input: What is the minimum password length, and is MFA required?
expected_output: Passwords must be at least 14 characters, unique to each system and stored only in the approved Northstar password manager. Multifactor authentication is mandatory for all Northstar systems.
context: Passwords must be at least 14 characters
MFA is mandatory for all systems.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
19 IT acceptable use, information security and AI usage > 19.2 Passwords, multifactor authentication and access control

Passwords must be at least **14 characters** , unique to each system and stored only in the approved Northstar password manager. Multifactor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all Northstar systems. Never share passwords or MFA codes, and never approve an MFA prompt you did not initiate. Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed quarterly by system owners.

IT Security, Data Protection and Generative AI Policy (NDS-SEC-ITG-004 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Acceptable use > 4.2 Passwords and multifactor authentication

- Minimum 14 characters; a passphrase of four or more random words is recommended.

- Unique for each system; stored only in the Northstar password manager.

- MFA is mandatory for all systems. Number-matching push or hardware security keys are required for privileged accounts.

- Never share passwords, MFA codes or session tokens, including with IT staff. IT will never ask for your password.

- Never approve an MFA request you did not start. Report unexpected MFA prompts as a security incident.

input: What is the annual learning budget per employee?
expected_output: Every employee has a learning budget of £1,000 per financial year (1 April to 31 March). It is not reduced for part-time employees, is pro-rated for mid-year joiners by complete months remaining, needs line manager pre-approval, and does not carry over.
context: Every employee has a learning budget of £1,000 per financial year (1 April to 31 March)
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
13 Performance management and development > 13.6 Training, certifications, mentoring and learning budgets

- Every employee has a **learning budget of £1,000 per financial year** (1 April to 31 March) for courses, conferences, books and certification exams relevant to their role or career framework. The budget is not reduced for part-time employees; for employees joining part-way through the financial year it is pro-rated by complete months remaining. Unused budget does not carry over.

- Spending from the learning budget requires line manager pre-approval in PeopleHub.

- Any single course or programme costing more than **£1,500** (which needs additional funding approved by the Head of Department) requires a study agreement. If the employee resigns within 12 months of completing it, they repay 100% of the cost if they leave within 6 months, and 50% if they leave between 6 and 12 months. Repayment does not apply if employment ends by redundancy.

- Certification exam fees are funded for the first attempt and one resit.

- Mandatory training (section 3.6) is repeated annually and must be completed by the published deadline.

- Northstar runs a mentoring programme with two intakes a year; any employee who has completed probation may apply to be a mentee.

input: I'm starting full-time next month — how much PTO will I get?
expected_output: Paid time off is called annual leave in Northstar policy. A full-time employee receives 27 days plus 8 bank holidays per leave year (1 January to 31 December). Because you are joining part-way through the year, your annual leave is pro-rated: 27 x calendar days employed / days in the year, rounded up to the nearest half day, plus the bank holidays that fall during your employment. During probation you can book accrued leave plus up to 2 extra days with approval.
context: Less than 3 years | 27 | 8 | 35
Pro-rated annual leave = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / total days in the leave year)
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.1 Annual leave entitlement

**Table 6.1 — Annual leave entitlement for full-time employees (37.5 hours per week, 5 days per week)**

|**Continuous service completed**|**Annual leave (days)**|**Bank holidays (days)**|**Total paid days off per leave**|
|---|---|---|---|
||||**year**|
|Less than 3 years|27|8|35|
|3 years or more, but less than 5 years|28|8|36|
|5 years or more|29|8|37|

- One day of annual leave equals **7.5 hours** for a full-time employee.

- The service-related increase applies from the **first 1 January that falls after** the date on which the employee completes the required continuous service. It is not applied part-way through a leave year.

- The entitlement applies to permanent and fixed-term employees, apprentices and interns. Part-time employees receive a pro-rated entitlement calculated in hours (section 6.3).

- Contractors and agency workers do not receive Northstar annual leave; agency workers' holiday is provided through their agency.

### **Statutory minimum holiday**

Almost all workers are legally entitled to 5.6 weeks' paid holiday per year, capped at 28 days for someone working 5 or more days a week. Employers may include bank holidays within the 5.6 weeks. Northstar's entitlement of 27 days plus 8 bank holidays (35 days for a full-time employee) exceeds the statutory minimum. No pro-rating or rounding rule in this handbook will ever reduce an employee's entitlement below the statutory minimum.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.4 Joining or leaving during the leave year

## **Joiner and leaver formula**

Pro-rated annual leave = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / total days in the leave year) Count calendar days inclusive of the start date and the leaving date. The leave year has 365 days (366 in a leap year; 2028 is the next leap year).

Rounding for full-time employees: round up to the nearest 0.5 day. Rounding for part-time employees (hours-based): round up to the nearest 0.25 hour.

Full-time joiners and leavers also receive, as paid days off, the bank holidays that fall during their employment. Part-time joiners and leavers use the hours-based allowance in section 6.3, pro-rated in the same way.

- **Joiner example:** a full-time employee starts on 1 March 2027. Calendar days employed in 2027 = 306 (1 March to 31 December inclusive). 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.64 days, rounded up to **23.0 days** of annual leave, plus the 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027 onwards.

- **Leaver example:** a full-time employee with less than 3 years' service leaves on 30 June 2027. Calendar days employed in 2027 = 181. 27 x 181 / 365 = 13.39 days, rounded up to **13.5 days** .

input: What's the cut-off for letting my boss know I'm off sick?
expected_output: You must call (phone or Teams call) your line manager no later than 09:30 on your first day of sickness; messages alone are not enough unless you physically cannot speak. Record the absence in PeopleHub the same day.
context: Text messages, emails or chat messages alone are not sufficient, except where you are physically unable to speak
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.1 Reporting an absence

### **How to report sickness**

1. **Call** your line manager (telephone or Teams voice/video call) no later than **09:30** on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least **1 hour before** their shift or rota period starts. 2. If your line manager is unavailable, call your Head of Department or team lead. Leaving a voicemail is acceptable only if you also send a message and follow up with a call before 12:00. 3. Text messages, emails or chat messages alone are not sufficient, except where you are physically unable to speak; in that case, send a message and call as soon as you are able. 4. Record the absence in PeopleHub on the same day, or ask your manager to do so on your behalf. 5. Tell your manager the reason for absence in general terms, your expected return date, and any work that needs urgent cover. You do not have to disclose a diagnosis.

input: My kid's nursery shut out of the blue today — what time off can I take?
expected_output: This is an emergency involving a dependant, covered by the statutory right to a reasonable amount of time off for dependants (unpaid by law, from day one). Northstar pays up to 2 working days per occurrence, up to 5 paid days per leave year; further time is unpaid or you may use annual leave. Call your line manager as soon as possible.
context: Northstar pays up to 2 working days per occurrence, up to a maximum of 5 paid days per leave year.
a breakdown in care arrangements
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.8 Time off for dependants, emergency leave and carer's leave

**Time off for dependants (statutory).** All employees may take a reasonable amount of time off to deal with an emergency involving a dependant — for example, a child falling ill, a breakdown in care arrangements, or a dependant being involved in an incident. A dependant can be a spouse, partner, child, grandchild, parent, or someone who depends on the employee for care. The right covers unexpected situations, not events the employee knew about in advance. There is no fixed limit; "reasonable" usually means enough time to deal with the immediate emergency and arrange alternative care. Statutory time off for dependants is unpaid.

**Northstar enhancement.** Northstar pays up to **2 working days per occurrence** , up to a maximum of **5 paid days per leave year** . Further time is unpaid, or the employee may choose to use annual leave.

**Carer's leave (statutory).** Employees can take up to **one week** of unpaid carer's leave in any 12-month period to give or arrange care for a dependant with a long-term care need. It is available from the first day of employment and can be taken in half days, individual days or a whole week. Notice must be at least 3 days for a half day or a full day, and at least twice the length of the leave for more than one day. No evidence of the dependant's care needs is required. **Northstar enhancement:** the first **3 days** of carer's leave in any rolling 12 months are paid at full basic pay.

input: My manager hasn't answered my holiday request — does that mean it's OK?
expected_output: Managers must decide within 5 working days. If there is no decision, PeopleHub automatically escalates the request to the Head of Department. A request is not approved by default because the manager did not respond, and you should not book non-refundable travel until it shows as Approved.
context: A request is not approved by default because a manager did not respond.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.7 Manager response, team coverage and critical delivery periods

- Managers must approve or decline a request in PeopleHub within **5 working days** of submission. If there is no decision after 5 working days, PeopleHub automatically escalates the request to the Head of Department. A request is not approved by default because a manager did not respond.

- Unless the Head of Department approves otherwise, no more than **30% of a team** (rounded down, with a minimum of one person) may be on planned annual leave on the same working day. For a team of 8 this is 2 people; for a team of 3 it is 1 person.

- A Head of Department may designate a **critical delivery period** (for example, a customer go-live, a data-centre migration or the Finance year-end close) by publishing it in PeopleHub at least **6 weeks** before it starts. A critical delivery period may last no more than **15 working days** , and no team may have more than **2** critical delivery periods in a leave year.

- Annual leave requested for dates within a published critical delivery period requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval, and will normally be approved only in exceptional circumstances.

- Leave that was already approved before a critical delivery period was published remains approved. It can only be cancelled by the company under section 6.13.

input: I'm in month 4 of my probation and was off sick for 4 days. Will I get company sick pay?
expected_output: Company sick pay depends on service: during probation the entitlement is SSP only. Since 6 April 2026 SSP is payable from the first day of sickness at the lower of £123.25 a week or 80% of normal weekly earnings, provided statutory conditions are met. You must have followed the reporting and self-certification rules.
context: During probation | SSP only | SSP only
SSP is payable from the first day of sickness absence
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.5 Company sick pay

Company sick pay is a contractual enhancement for employees whose contract incorporates the company sick pay scheme (all permanent and fixed-term employment contracts issued from 1 January 2025). It is paid **inclusive of SSP** : SSP forms part of, and is not paid in addition to, company sick pay.

**Table 7.5 — Company sick pay entitlement in any rolling 12-month period**

|**Continuous service on the first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Then half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed and less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more but less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

- The rolling 12-month period is the 12 months ending on the day before the first day of the current absence. Company sick pay already paid in that period is deducted from the entitlement.

- "Half pay" is half of basic pay; where half pay would be less than SSP, SSP is paid instead. After company sick pay is exhausted, SSP continues if the statutory conditions are met.

- Weeks are calculated by reference to the employee's normal working days (for example, one week for a 3-day-per-week employee is 3 working days).

- Company sick pay is conditional on following the reporting procedure in section 7.1 and providing the evidence in section 7.3. If the employee does not follow these steps without a good reason, company sick pay may be withheld for the affected days. Statutory Sick Pay is still paid where the statutory conditions are met.

- Contractors and agency workers are not eligible for company sick pay.

**Example.** An employee with 3 years' continuous service has received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months. They are now absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay entitlement = 8 − 5 = 3 weeks. They

therefore receive 3 weeks at full pay followed by 3 weeks at half pay (they have 8 weeks of half-pay entitlement available).

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.4 Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)

## **Statutory Sick Pay from 6 April 2026**

Following the Employment Rights Act 2025, from 6 April 2026 SSP is payable from the first day of sickness absence (the former 3 unpaid "waiting days" were removed) and the lower earnings limit no longer applies to eligibility. The weekly rate is £123.25 or 80% of the employee's normal weekly earnings, whichever is lower, for up to 28 weeks. Northstar's qualifying days for SSP are the employee's contracted working days. SSP rates are set by government and usually change each April.

input: I joined Northstar 2 months before my partner's due date. Can I take paternity leave, and will it be paid?
expected_output: Paternity leave is a day-one right since 6 April 2026, so you may take up to 2 weeks (one block or two 1-week blocks, ending within 52 weeks of the birth), provided you give notice of the due date at least 15 weeks before it (or as soon as reasonably practicable given your start date — confirm with People Operations). Statutory Paternity Pay and Northstar's full-pay enhancement both require 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth, so with about 2 months' service you are not eligible; the leave is unpaid, but you may use annual leave instead.
context: Since 6 April 2026, paternity leave is a day-one right for eligible employees.
Employees who are entitled to paternity leave but do not qualify for SPP (for example, because they joined less than 26 weeks before the qualifying week) take paternity leave unpaid
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.2 Paternity leave and pay

**Leave.** Since 6 April 2026, paternity leave is a day-one right for eligible employees. An employee who is the biological father of the child, or the partner of the mother or adopter, and who expects to have responsibility for the child's upbringing, may take up to **2 weeks** of paternity leave, as one 2-week block or two separate 1-week blocks. Leave cannot start before the birth and must end within 52 weeks of the birth (or of the due date if the baby is born early).

**Notice.** The employee must tell People Operations the due date at least 15 weeks before the baby is due, and must give 28 days' notice to change the start date of paternity leave.

**Statutory Paternity Pay.** SPP is £194.32 per week or 90% of AWE, whichever is lower. It requires at least 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the qualifying week (the 15th week before the EWC), continued employment up to the date of birth, and AWE of at least £129.

**Northstar enhancement.** Employees who qualify for SPP receive **full basic pay for 2 weeks** , inclusive of SPP. Employees who are entitled to paternity leave but do not qualify for SPP (for example, because they joined less than 26 weeks before the qualifying week) take paternity leave unpaid; they may choose to use annual leave instead for some or all of the period.

**Statutory Paternity Pay.** SPP is £194.32 per week or 90% of AWE, whichever is lower. It requires at least 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the qualifying week (the 15th week before the EWC), continued employment up to the date of birth, and AWE of at least £129.

**Northstar enhancement.** Employees who qualify for SPP receive **full basic pay for 2 weeks** , inclusive of SPP. Employees who are entitled to paternity leave but do not qualify for SPP (for example, because they joined less than 26 weeks before the qualifying week) take paternity leave unpaid; they may choose to use annual leave instead for some or all of the period.

input: What conditions must I meet to get Northstar's enhanced maternity pay, and what does it pay?
expected_output: Enhanced maternity pay requires that you qualify for SMP (including average weekly earnings of at least £129) and have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth. It pays full basic pay (inclusive of SMP) for weeks 1–16, SMP only for weeks 17–39, and nothing for weeks 40–52. If you do not return for at least 6 months after maternity leave, the enhanced element above SMP is repayable, except for redundancy, ill-health capability or a further immediately following period of statutory family leave. Maternity leave itself (52 weeks) is a day-one right.
context: Employees who qualify for SMP and have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the EWC receive:
Weeks 1 to 16 | Full basic pay, inclusive of SMP or SAP.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.1 Maternity leave and pay

**Leave.** Pregnant employees are entitled to up to 52 weeks of Statutory Maternity Leave (26 weeks of Ordinary Maternity Leave and 26 weeks of Additional Maternity Leave), regardless of length of service, hours or pay. The earliest leave can start is 11 weeks before the EWC. Employees must take at least 2 weeks of compulsory maternity leave after the birth.

**Notice.** By the end of the 15th week before the EWC, the employee must tell People Operations (via PeopleHub) that she is pregnant, her EWC and the date she wants maternity leave to start. Northstar will confirm the expected return date in writing within 28 days. To change the return date, the employee must give at least 8 weeks' notice.

**Statutory Maternity Pay.** SMP requires at least 28 days' notice of the date SMP should start and evidence of pregnancy (a MATB1 certificate or a letter from a doctor or midwife) within 21 days of the SMP start date. A MATB1 cannot be issued more than 20 weeks before the due date. Employees who do not qualify for SMP may be able to claim Maternity Allowance from the government; Northstar will issue form SMP1 explaining why SMP is not payable.

**Northstar enhanced maternity pay.** Employees who qualify for SMP **and** have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the EWC receive:

**Table 8.1 — Northstar enhanced maternity and adoption pay**

|**Weeks of leave**|**Payment**|
|---|---|
|Weeks 1 to 16|Full basic pay, inclusive of SMP or SAP.|
|Weeks 17 to 39|SMP or SAP only.|
|Weeks 40 to 52|Unpaid.|

If the employee does not return to work for at least **6 months** after the end of maternity leave, she must repay the enhanced element (the amount paid above SMP), unless employment ends because of redundancy, ill-health capability, or a further period of statutory family leave immediately following the first. Statutory pay is never repayable because an employee does not return.

input: I've worked here 4 years. Could I take a 2-month sabbatical starting in 14 months' time?
expected_output: Sabbaticals are discretionary unpaid leave of 1 to 3 months for employees who will have at least 5 years' continuous service on the proposed start date, no more than once in 5 years. Applications must be made at least 3 months before the start and are approved by a Director depending on business needs. In 14 months you will have roughly 5 years and 2 months' service, so you can apply, but approval is not guaranteed; salary, pension contributions and annual leave accrual are suspended during the unpaid period.

input: I resigned in June. Will I still get the annual bonus paid in July?
expected_output: The Annual Performance Bonus is discretionary and non-contractual. To be considered, an employee must have joined on or before 31 December of the financial year and be employed, and not under notice given or received, on the payment date in July. Having resigned in June, you would be under notice (or have left) at the July payment date, so you would not be eligible.

retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.7 Bonuses and variable pay

Northstar operates a discretionary **Annual Performance Bonus** for the financial year 1 April to 31 March, paid in July. The scheme is non-contractual: the company decides whether a bonus pool exists and the amount of any individual award. To be considered, an employee must have joined on or before 31 December of the financial year concerned and be employed, and not under notice given or received, on the payment date. Awards are pro-rated for part-time employees and for part-year service. Receiving a bonus in one year creates no entitlement in future years.

input: Can I carry over more than 5 days of leave this year?
expected_output: The standard limit is 5 days, used by 31 March. More can be carried only if: (a) sickness prevented you taking leave — up to 4 weeks extra, to be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year; (b) family-related leave prevented it — all untaken leave, to be used within 12 months of return; or (c) the company asked you to defer for business reasons — a further 5 days (10 total), requested by 30 November, approved by the Director of People Operations, used by 30 June. Exceptions are not automatic and not precedents.

input: I'm a G2 engineer and I've just resigned. I have 5 days of approved leave booked for after my last day. What happens?
expected_output: As a G2 after probation your contractual notice is 1 month. Approved leave that falls after your leaving date is cancelled automatically. Your final holiday balance is the pro-rated entitlement to the leaving date plus valid carryover minus leave taken or booked; positive balances are paid at annual basic salary / 260 per day, and over-taken leave is deducted where the contract permits. You may ask to take leave during your notice period, and Northstar may require you to take accrued leave during notice by giving notice of at least twice the length of that leave. Final adjustments are paid per the final pay timing rule (section 22.11).
context: Approved leave that falls after the employee's leaving date is cancelled automatically.
After probation, grades G1 to G3 | 1 month
Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.16 Leave during probation, negative balances and leave during notice periods

**Probation.** During probation an employee may book leave that will have accrued by the first day of the leave (the annual entitlement x complete calendar months of service / 12, rounded up to the nearest 0.5 day) plus up to **2 additional days** with line manager approval. Leave of more than 5 consecutive working days during probation also requires Head of Department approval.

**Negative balances.** After probation, an employee may book their full annual entitlement in advance. With Head of Department approval, an employee may also borrow up to **3 days** from the next leave year in exceptional circumstances. If employment ends when an employee has taken more leave than they have accrued, the excess is deducted from final pay at the daily rate in section 6.17, where the employment contract contains a written deduction clause (all Northstar contracts issued on or after 1 January 2025 contain this clause) or the employee has given prior written consent.

**Notice periods.** Employees serving notice may request leave in the normal way. Northstar may require an employee to take some or all of their accrued but untaken leave during their notice period by giving notice of at least twice the length of the leave to be taken. Approved leave that falls after the employee's leaving date is cancelled automatically. During garden leave (section 22.6), Northstar may require accrued leave to be taken.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.4 Notice periods **Table 22.4 — Notice periods** |**Situation**|**Notice the employee must give (contractual)**|**Notice Northstar must give**| |---|---|---| |During probation|1 week|1 week| |After probation, grades G1 to G3|1 month|The greater of 1 month and the statutory
minimum| |After probation, grades G4 and G5|2 months|The greater of 2 months and the statutory
minimum| |After probation, grades G6 and G7|3 months|The greater of 3 months and the statutory
minimum| ## **Statutory minimum notice** An employee with more than 1 month's service must give at least 1 week's notice. An employer must give at least 1 week's notice to an employee with between 1 month and 2 years' service, then 1 week for each complete year of service from 2 years, up to a maximum of 12 weeks after 12 years. A contract can give more than these minimums but never less. Notice periods in Table 22.4 are illustrative Northstar contractual terms; the individual employment contract prevails. **Example.** Northstar gives notice to a G2 engineer with 9 complete years of service. Contractual notice is 1 month; statutory notice is 9 weeks. Northstar must give **9 weeks** ' notice because it is longer. If the same engineer resigns, they need give only their contractual notice of 1 month.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.17 Termination and final holiday balance

### **Final holiday balance formula**

Final balance (days) = pro-rated entitlement for the leave year up to the leaving date (section 6.4) + valid carried-over leave − leave taken or booked up to the leaving date

Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260

Hourly rate for payment or deduction (part-time and hours-based calculations) = annual basic salary / (52 x contracted weekly hours)

**Example — positive balance.** A full-time employee earning £45,500 per year leaves on 30 June 2027 with no carried-over leave and has taken 10 days. Pro-rated entitlement = 13.5 days (section 6.4). Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Payment = 3.5 x (£45,500 / 260) = 3.5 x £175.00 = **£612.50** gross, paid in the final salary payment.

**Example — negative balance.** If the same employee had taken 15 days, the balance would be 13.5 − 15 = −1.5 days. Deduction = 1.5 x £175.00 = **£262.50** gross, deducted from final pay where the contract permits (section 6.16).

input: Can I take 3 days off during a customer go-live that my Head of Department has published as a critical delivery period?
expected_output: Critical delivery periods must be published at least 6 weeks ahead, last at most 15 working days and no more than 2 per team per year. Leave within one requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval and is normally approved only in exceptional circumstances (for example, a family wedding booked before publication). The normal 10-working-day notice for 2–5 days still applies. Leave approved before publication remains approved and can only be cancelled by the company in exceptional circumstances with re-credit and reimbursement of evidenced non-refundable costs.
context: Annual leave requested for dates within a published critical delivery period requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval, and will normally be approved only in exceptional circumstances.
More than 1 and up to 5 working days | 10 working days | Line manager
Leave approved before publication stays approved unless cancelled under handbook section 6.13
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.7 Manager response, team coverage and critical delivery periods

- Managers must approve or decline a request in PeopleHub within **5 working days** of submission. If there is no decision after 5 working days, PeopleHub automatically escalates the request to the Head of Department. A request is not approved by default because a manager did not respond.

- Unless the Head of Department approves otherwise, no more than **30% of a team** (rounded down, with a minimum of one person) may be on planned annual leave on the same working day. For a team of 8 this is 2 people; for a team of 3 it is 1 person.

- A Head of Department may designate a **critical delivery period** (for example, a customer go-live, a data-centre migration or the Finance year-end close) by publishing it in PeopleHub at least **6 weeks** before it starts. A critical delivery period may last no more than **15 working days** , and no team may have more than **2** critical delivery periods in a leave year.

- Annual leave requested for dates within a published critical delivery period requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval, and will normally be approved only in exceptional circumstances.

- Leave that was already approved before a critical delivery period was published remains approved. It can only be cancelled by the company under section 6.13.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.6 Requesting leave and minimum notice All annual leave must be requested in PeopleHub and approved before it is taken. Leave is not approved until it shows as "Approved" in PeopleHub. Employees should not book non-refundable travel before approval. **Table 6.6 — Minimum notice for annual leave requests (requests submitted on or after 1 October 2026)** |**Length of leave requested**|**Minimum notice**|**Approver**| |---|---|---| |Up to 1 working day (including hourly and
half-day leave)|2 working days|Line manager| |More than 1 and up to 5 working days|10 working days|Line manager| |More than 5 and up to 10 working days|20 working days|Line manager| |More than 10 and up to 15 consecutive working
days|40 working days|Line manager and Head of Department| |More than 15 consecutive working days|40 working days|Line manager, Head of Department and
Director| **How notice is counted.** Notice is the number of working days between the date the request is submitted in PeopleHub and the first day of leave, counting neither the submission date nor the first day of leave. Bank holidays are not working days. Managers may approve requests made with shorter notice at their discretion where cover allows. Short-notice approval is discretionary and is not an entitlement. Emergency situations are covered by section 9.2 (emergency leave and time off for dependants), not by annual leave rules.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.7 Critical delivery periods and team coverage

A Head of Department may publish a critical delivery period in PeopleHub at least 6 weeks before it starts, lasting no more than 15 working days, with no more than 2 per team per leave year. During that period, annual leave also requires Head of Department approval and is approved only exceptionally (for example, a family wedding booked before the period was published, or compassionate reasons). Leave approved before publication stays approved unless cancelled under handbook section 6.13, with re-credit of the leave and reimbursement of evidenced non-refundable costs.

input: I'm going from full-time to 22.5 hours (Mon–Wed) on 1 July 2027 and I've already taken 60 hours of leave this year. How is my 2027 leave worked out?
expected_output: Under the changed-hours method you split the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded, add them, round up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays falling on working days. Period 1 (1 Jan–30 Jun, 181 days, full-time): 262.5 x 181/365 = 130.171 h. Period 2 (1 Jul–31 Dec, 184 days, 0.6 FTE): 157.5 x 184/365 = 79.397 h. Total 209.568 → 209.75 h. Bank holidays: period 1 has 5 on working days (37.5 h), period 2 has 3 on Mon–Wed (22.5 h). Bookable = 149.75 h; after 60 h taken, 89.75 h remain, of which 7.5 h is reserved for the shutdown day on Wednesday 29 December 2027.
context: Bookable annual leave for 2027: 209.75 − 37.5 − 22.5 = 149.75 hours
Add the unrounded results together and then round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour.

- Period 2: 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397 hours

input: I'm going to Berlin for 3 nights for a customer workshop. What approvals do I need and how do I claim a taxi I paid for in cash euros?
expected_output: International travel requires Director pre-approval and a Travel desk travel-risk check before booking, and an overnight stay is involved. Berlin is Band B: hotel up to £200 per night, breakfast £15, lunch £20, dinner £45, daily meal cap £70, incidental £10 per night. Claims are in sterling: card payments use the statement amount including fees; cash uses Finance's published monthly rate for the month of the expense, sterling = foreign amount / rate rounded to the nearest penny (e.g. €30 / 1.16 = £25.86). Itemised receipts are needed and the claim must be submitted within 30 days; a total over £250 requires line manager and Head of Department approval.

input: I got ill on the second day of my holiday in New York. What should I do to get my leave back?
expected_output: Sickness during annual leave can be reclassified and re-credited if you report it on the first day of sickness by calling your line manager by 09:30, or as soon as reasonably practicable if you are in a different time zone, and provide evidence: self-certification for up to 7 calendar days or a fit note for more than 7. Sickness reported only after you return is not normally reclassified. Reclassified days are paid as sickness absence.
context: report the sickness to their line manager by 09:30 on the first day of sickness (or as soon as reasonably practicable if they are in a different time zone)
Days of sickness reported only after the employee returns from leave will not normally be reclassified.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.12 Sickness during annual leave

An employee who falls ill during annual leave may have the affected days reclassified as sickness absence and re-credited to their annual leave balance, provided that they:

1. report the sickness to their line manager by **09:30** on the first day of sickness (or as soon as reasonably practicable if they are in a different time zone), following section 7.1; and

2. provide self-certification for absences of up to 7 calendar days, or a fit note for absences of more than 7 calendar days, as set out in section 7.3.

Days of sickness reported only after the employee returns from leave will not normally be reclassified. Reclassified days are paid as sickness absence under section 7.

input: I'm a remote employee and my last day is Friday 20 November 2026. What are my deadlines for returning equipment and submitting expenses, when is my access cut off, and when will my final holiday pay arrive?
expected_output: Remote or hybrid leavers return equipment within 5 working days after the leaving date: 23–27 November, so by Friday 27 November 2026. Expense claims must be submitted within 10 working days after the leaving date: by Friday 4 December 2026. System and building access is revoked at 17:30 on the last working day. Because the leaving date is after the 10th, November salary is paid as normal on 25 November and final adjustments are paid on the 25th of the following month; 25 December 2026 is Christmas Day (a bank holiday), so payment is on the previous working day, Thursday 24 December 2026.
context: Remote or hybrid leavers return all equipment within 5 working days after their leaving date
Leavers must submit all claims within 10 working days after their leaving date.
If the leaving date is after the 10th, normal salary for that month is paid on the 25th and the final adjustments (holiday pay, expenses and deductions) are paid on the 25th of the following month.
If the 25th falls on a weekend or bank holiday, salary is paid on the previous working day.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
20 Company equipment and property > 20.6 Returning equipment

### **Equipment return deadlines**

- **Office-based leavers** return all equipment and their access card to IT on their **last working day** .

- **Remote or hybrid leavers** return all equipment within **5 working days** after their leaving date, using the prepaid courier arranged by IT. Access cards may be posted with the equipment.

- If equipment has not been returned within **10 working days** after the leaving date, IT escalates to People Operations, who send a written reminder and may take recovery action. Any deduction from final pay is made only where the contract permits or the employee has agreed in writing.

- Employees returning from long-term absence or moving role return any equipment no longer needed within 10 working days of IT's request.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
12 Expenses and business travel > 12.3 Claim deadline and late claims

## **Expense claim deadline**

Submit claims in ExpenseFlow within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted 31 to 90 calendar days after the expense require a written explanation and Head of Department approval. Claims submitted more than 90 calendar days after the expense are not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the employee was on long-term sickness absence). Leavers must submit all claims within **10 working days** after their leaving date.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.11 Final pay and outstanding annual leave

Salary is paid for the calendar month on the 25th (section 11.1). If the leaving date is **on or before** the 10th of a month, all final pay, including payment for untaken annual leave, approved expenses and any deductions, is paid on the 25th of that month. If the leaving date is **after** the 10th, normal salary for that month is paid on the 25th and the final adjustments (holiday pay, expenses and deductions) are paid on the 25th of the following month. The final holiday balance is calculated as set out in section 6.17.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.1 Salary payment

Salaries are paid monthly, for the calendar month, by bank transfer on the **25th of each month** . If the 25th falls on a weekend or bank holiday, salary is paid on the previous working day.

input: A customer made sexual comments to me during a meeting at their site. What can I do and how fast must I report it?
expected_output: Northstar protects employees from harassment by customers and third parties. You may end the call or meeting, or leave the location if you feel unsafe, and you will not be penalised for doing so in good faith. Harassment from a customer is Severity 2: report to your line manager and the relevant team within 1 hour. Record what happened and keep evidence. Your manager will ensure you are safe, offer support and escalate to the Account Director and People Operations; Northstar will raise it with the customer and may change staffing or suspend services.
context: may end the call or meeting, or leave the location if they feel unsafe
Harassment, threats or abuse from a customer; injury needing medical treatment; confirmed exposure of Confidential information
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
21 Complaints involving customers and workplace incidents > 21.3 Inappropriate customer behaviour

Northstar protects employees from harassment by customers and other third parties. An employee who experiences abusive, discriminatory or sexually inappropriate behaviour from a customer may end the call or meeting, or leave the location if they feel unsafe, and must report it under Table 21.2. The line manager will make sure the employee is safe, offer support, and escalate to the Account Director and People Operations. input: I've been summoned for jury service during my team's critical delivery period. Do I have to go, and will I be paid?
expected_output: Jury service is a statutory right to time off, not annual leave, so critical-delivery-period rules on annual leave do not apply. Tell your manager and upload the summons within 2 working days. If the absence would seriously harm the business Northstar may ask you to apply to defer, giving you a letter; deferral is possible only once in 12 months. Northstar pays full basic pay for the first 10 working days in a leave year (do not claim loss of earnings for those days); after that it is unpaid and you claim loss of earnings from the court.
context: Northstar must allow employees time off for jury service.
Northstar pays full basic pay for the first 10 working days of jury service in any leave year
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
9 Other forms of leave > 9.3 Jury service

Northstar must allow employees time off for jury service. Employees must tell their line manager and upload a copy of the summons to PeopleHub within **2 working days** of receiving it. If the absence would seriously harm the business, Northstar may ask the employee to apply to defer jury service, giving the employee a letter explaining why; jury service can be deferred only once in a 12-month period. Northstar pays full basic pay for the first **10 working days** of jury service in any leave year; the employee must not claim loss of earnings from the court for those days. After 10 working days, jury service is unpaid by Northstar and the employee may claim loss of earnings from the court using the court's employer form, which People Operations will complete.

input: I'm starting a hybrid role on 1 March 2027. How often must I be in the office at first, how much leave can I book by June, and when can I claim the home office allowance?
expected_output: New starters in hybrid roles attend at least 3 days a week for their first 4 weeks, then follow the standard of 8 days per rolling 4-week period. During probation you may book accrued leave (27 x 3/12 = 6.75, rounded up to 7.0 days on 1 June) plus up to 2 days with manager approval: 9.0 days; more than 5 consecutive days also needs Head of Department approval. The £300 home office allowance is available only after completing the 6-month probation, i.e. from 1 September 2027 if probation is passed on time.
context: new starters in hybrid roles attend at least 3 days per week to complete induction
With line manager approval they may book up to 7.0 + 2 = 9.0 days
After completing probation, employees may claim a home office allowance of up to £300

3 Annual leave > 3.2 Accrual and booking

input: I'm pregnant and have had several pregnancy-related sick days. Will they count towards attendance triggers?
expected_output: Pregnancy-related sickness is recorded separately and never counted towards attendance triggers or used in performance, promotion or redundancy decisions. You have a statutory right to reasonable paid time off for antenatal care, and your manager should carry out a pregnancy risk assessment. If you are off with a pregnancy-related illness in the 4 weeks before the expected week of childbirth, maternity leave and pay may start automatically.
context: Pregnancy-related absence is excluded from all triggers.
never counted towards attendance triggers
Pregnant employees have a statutory right to reasonable paid time off for antenatal care

7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.9 Disability, pregnancy and mental health

- **Disability-related absence:** handled with reasonable adjustments (section 4.3). Absence connected with an agreed adjustment (for example, scheduled treatment) may be recorded as disability leave rather than sickness absence.

- **Pregnancy-related sickness:** recorded separately and never counted towards attendance triggers or used in decisions about performance, promotion or redundancy. If a pregnant employee is absent with a pregnancy-related illness in the 4 weeks before the expected week of childbirth, maternity leave and pay may start automatically (see section 8.1).

- **Mental health:** treated in the same way as physical illness. Employees can access the Employee Assistance Programme (Appendix B) and agree a Wellness Action Plan with their manager.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.7 Pregnancy and adoption appointments

- Pregnant employees have a statutory right to reasonable **paid** time off for antenatal care, including relaxation and parenting classes recommended by a doctor or midwife. After the first appointment, Northstar may ask to see an appointment card and confirmation of pregnancy.

- Partners of a pregnant woman have a statutory right to unpaid time off to accompany her to up to two antenatal appointments, of up to 6.5 hours each. Northstar pays this time in full as a company enhancement.

- Employees adopting a child can take time off for adoption appointments in line with the statutory scheme; Northstar pays this time in full.

input: I work 3 days a week (Mon–Wed, 7.5 hours a day) and have less than 3 years' service. How many hours of annual leave can I book in 2027?
expected_output: Part-time allowance = 262.5 x (22.5 / 37.5) = 157.5 hours including bank holidays. In 2027 six bank holidays fall on Monday–Wednesday (29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May, 30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) = 6 x 7.5 = 45 hours. Bookable annual leave = 157.5 − 45 = 112.5 hours (15 days of 7.5 hours).

6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours

Part-time employees' entitlement is calculated in hours and includes the bank holiday element, so that part-time employees are treated no less favourably than full-time employees, whichever days they work.

For employees with 3 or more years' service the full-time total is 270 hours (36 days); with 5 or more years it is 277.5 hours (37 days). Bank holidays that fall on the employee's normal working days are deducted from the allowance, at the hours the employee would normally have worked that day. 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours

## **Part-time entitlement formula**

In 2027 the bank holidays in England and Wales fall on Friday 1 January, Friday 26 March, Monday 29 March, Monday 3 May, Monday 31 May, Monday 30 August, Monday 27 December and Tuesday 28 December. An employee working Monday to Wednesday therefore has 6 bank holidays on working days (29 March, 3 May, 31 May, 30 August, 27 December and 28 December).

**Changes to working hours part-way through the leave year.** Where contracted hours change during the leave year, divide the leave year into periods at the date of change. Calculate the allowance for each period as: (annual allowance in hours for that working pattern) x (calendar days in the period / days in the leave year). Add the unrounded results together and then round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour. Deduct bank holidays that fell on working days in each period at the hours worked on that day in that period. Leave already taken in the first period is deducted from the new total. Worked examples are in NDS-HR-LAS-002 section 3.4.

Compressed hours employees (for example, 37.5 hours worked over 4 days) are 1.0 FTE and receive 262.5 hours, with each bank holiday on a working day deducted at the length of that working day (9.375 hours on a 4-day compressed week).

Add the unrounded results together and then round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour. Deduct bank holidays that fell on working days in each period at the hours worked on that day in that period. Leave already taken in the first period is deducted from the new total. Worked examples are in NDS-HR-LAS-002 section 3.4.

Compressed hours employees (for example, 37.5 hours worked over 4 days) are 1.0 FTE and receive 262.5 hours, with each bank holiday on a working day deducted at the length of that working day (9.375 hours on a 4-day compressed week).

input: A full-time employee earning £45,500 leaves on 30 June 2027 having taken 10 days of leave and with no carryover. What holiday pay is due?
expected_output: Pro-rated entitlement = 27 x 181/365 = 13.389, rounded up to 13.5 days. Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Daily rate = £45,500 / 260 = £175.00. Payment = 3.5 x £175.00 = £612.50 gross. Because 30 June is after the 10th, it is paid with final adjustments on 25 July 2027.
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.17 Termination and final holiday balance

### **Final holiday balance formula**

Final balance (days) = pro-rated entitlement for the leave year up to the leaving date (section 6.4) + valid carried-over leave − leave taken or booked up to the leaving date

Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260

Hourly rate for payment or deduction (part-time and hours-based calculations) = annual basic salary / (52 x contracted weekly hours)

**Example — positive balance.** A full-time employee earning £45,500 per year leaves on 30 June 2027 with no carried-over leave and has taken 10 days. Pro-rated entitlement = 13.5 days (section 6.4). Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Payment = 3.5 x (£45,500 / 260) = 3.5 x £175.00 = **£612.50** gross, paid in the final salary payment.

**Example — negative balance.** If the same employee had taken 15 days, the balance would be 13.5 − 15 = −1.5 days. Deduction = 1.5 x £175.00 = **£262.50** gross, deducted from final pay where the contract permits (section 6.16).

input: Someone works 22.5 hours (Mon–Wed) from 1 January to 31 March 2027 and then full-time for the rest of the year. What is their bookable annual leave for 2027?
expected_output: Period 1 (90 days, part-time): 157.5 x 90/365 = 38.836 h. Period 2 (275 days, full-time): 262.5 x 275/365 = 197.774 h. Total 236.610 h, rounded up to 236.75 h. Bank holidays on working days: 29 March in period 1 (7.5 h) and 3 May, 31 May, 30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec in period 2 (37.5 h) = 45 h. Bookable = 236.75 − 45 = 191.75 hours.
context: Bookable annual leave for 2027: 236.75 − 45 = 191.75 hours
retrieval_context:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

Divide the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded as (annual allowance for that pattern) x (calendar days in period / days in year), add the periods, round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays on working days for each period.

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

- Period 1: 262.5 x 181 / 365 = 130.171 hours

- Period 2: 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397 hours

- Total: 209.568 hours, rounded up to **209.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days, period 1 (1 Jan, 26 Mar, 29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May): 5 x 7.5 = 37.5 hours

- Bank holidays on working days, period 2 (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec): 3 x 7.5 = 22.5 hours

- Bookable annual leave for 2027: 209.75 − 37.5 − 22.5 = **149.75 hours**

- If the employee took 60 hours of annual leave in period 1, the remaining balance from 1 July is 149.75 − 60 = **89.75 hours** , of which 7.5 hours must be reserved for the shutdown day that falls on a working day (Wednesday 29 December 2027).

input: An employee in probation, whose normal weekly earnings are above £154.07, is off sick for 4 working days (5-day week). How much sick pay do they receive?
expected_output: During probation only SSP is paid. SSP is payable from the first day since 6 April 2026 at £123.25 a week (lower than 80% of earnings above £154.07). Daily rate = £123.25 / 5 qualifying days = £24.65. 4 days x £24.65 = £98.60.
retrieval_context:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.4 Company sick pay

**Table 4.4 — Company sick pay (inclusive of SSP) in any rolling 12 months**

|**Continuous service on first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed, less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more, less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

## **Worked examples 4.4 — sick pay**

- **Probation:** a full-time employee in probation (normal weekly earnings above £154.07, so the £123.25 rate applies) is absent for 4 working days. Daily SSP = £123.25 / 5 = £24.65. SSP payable = 4 x £24.65 = **£98.60** . No company sick pay is due.

- **3 years' service:** an employee who has already received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months is absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay weeks = 8 − 5 = 3. They receive 3 weeks at full pay and 3 weeks at half pay.

- **6 years' service, salary £52,000, no previous sick pay in 12 months, absent 15 weeks:** 13 weeks at full pay (£1,000 per week) and 2 weeks at half pay (£500 per week, which is more than SSP). Pay for weeks 14 and 15 = 2 x £500 = **£1,000** .

Company sick pay may be withheld for days where the reporting or evidence rules were not followed without good reason; SSP remains payable where the statutory conditions are met.

input: For a one-night London trip: rail £84, hotel £195 room-only, day 1 lunch £14 and dinner £38 (including a £6 glass of wine), day 2 breakfast £13 and lunch £16, plus the incidental allowance. How much is reimbursed and who approves?
expected_output: Rail £84.00 in full. Hotel capped at the London limit £180.00. Day 1: wine is not reimbursable so dinner is £32.00; lunch £14.00; total £46.00 (under £55 cap). Day 2: breakfast capped at £12.00, lunch capped at £15.00 = £27.00. Incidental £5.00. Total £84 + £180 + £46 + £27 + £5 = £342.00. Claim value £250.01–£1,000 needs line manager and Head of Department approval.
retrieval_context:
Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.1 — two-day London trip**

A Manchester-based consultant travels to London on Tuesday and returns Wednesday, with an approved overnight stay.

- Standard-class return rail: £84.00 — reimbursed in full.

- Hotel: £195.00 room only — limit £180.00; £180.00 reimbursed (the £15.00 excess is not reimbursed unless the Head of Department approves an exception, which is within the 25% threshold).

- Tuesday: lunch £14.00 and dinner £38.00 including a £6.00 glass of wine. Wine is not reimbursable, so dinner = £32.00. Tuesday meals = £46.00 (within the £55 daily cap).

- Wednesday: breakfast £13.00 (limit £12.00) and lunch £16.00 (limit £15.00). Wednesday meals = £27.00.

- Incidental allowance: £5.00.

- **Total reimbursed: £84.00 + £180.00 + £46.00 + £27.00 + £5.00 = £342.00.** Because the claim is between £250.01 and £1,000.00, it requires line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.2 — daily meal cap**

On a day of an overnight UK trip, an employee spends £12.00 on breakfast, £15.00 on lunch and £35.00 on dinner. Each item is within its individual limit, but the total of £62.00 exceeds the £55.00 daily cap, so **£55.00** is reimbursed.

## **Example 14.3 — mileage with commuting deduction**

An employee whose normal workplace is the Manchester office (12 miles from home) drives from home to a customer site in Leeds (50 miles from home) and back. Business miles = (50 − 12) x 2 = 76 miles. They have claimed fewer than 10,000 business miles this tax year. Reimbursement = 76 x £0.55 = **£41.80** .

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.4 — crossing the 10,000-mile threshold**

An employee has already claimed 9,950 business miles in the 2026/27 tax year and makes a 120-mile business journey. The first 50 miles are paid at 55p and the remaining 70 at 25p: (50 x £0.55) + (70 x £0.25) = £27.50 + £17.50 = **£45.00** .

## **Example 14.5 — Berlin trip (Band B), currency conversion**

An employee travels to Berlin for 3 nights with Director pre-approval and a travel-risk check. The hotel costs €210 per night on the corporate card; the card statement shows £181.50 per night including fees, which is within the £200 Band B limit, so £544.50 is reimbursed for 3 nights. A taxi costing €30 was paid in cash; Finance's published rate for that month is 1.16 euros per £1, so the claim is €30 / 1.16 = **£25.86** . Because the total claim exceeds £250, it needs line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.6 — client dinner**

A dinner for 4 people (2 client attendees and 2 Northstar employees) costs £296.00 including drinks, which is £74.00 per head. This is above the £60 per head limit by 23%, so the Head of Department (who must pre-approve all client entertainment) may approve the excess as an exception up to 25% above the limit. If the bill had been £320.00 (£80.00 per head, 33% above the limit), Director approval would be required for the excess. Neither amount exceeds £100 per head, so no gifts and hospitality register entry is required.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

# **Example 14.7 — late claims and reimbursement dates**

- An expense incurred on Wednesday 3 March 2027 and submitted on Thursday 15 April 2027 is 43 calendar days old: a late claim needing a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- The same expense submitted on Saturday 5 June 2027 would be 94 calendar days old and would not be reimbursed unless the Finance Director approved an exception.

- A claim fully approved on 9 March 2027 is paid on Thursday 25 March 2027. A claim fully approved on 12 March 2027 is paid in the April payroll; because 25 April 2027 is a Sunday, it is paid on Friday 23 April 2027.

- Standard-class return rail: £84.00 — reimbursed in full.

- Hotel: £195.00 room only — limit £180.00; £180.00 reimbursed (the £15.00 excess is not reimbursed unless the Head of Department approves an exception, which is within the 25% threshold).

- Tuesday: lunch £14.00 and dinner £38.00 including a £6.00 glass of wine. Wine is not reimbursable, so dinner = £32.00. Tuesday meals = £46.00 (within the £55 daily cap).

- Wednesday: breakfast £13.00 (limit £12.00) and lunch £16.00 (limit £15.00). Wednesday meals = £27.00.

- Incidental allowance: £5.00.

- **Total reimbursed: £84.00 + £180.00 + £46.00 + £27.00 + £5.00 = £342.00.** Because the claim is between £250.01 and £1,000.00, it requires line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.2 — daily meal cap**

On a day of an overnight UK trip, an employee spends £12.00 on breakfast, £15.00 on lunch and £35.00 on dinner. Each item is within its individual limit, but the total of £62.00 exceeds the £55.00 daily cap, so **£55.00** is reimbursed.

## **Example 14.3 — mileage with commuting deduction**

An employee whose normal workplace is the Manchester office (12 miles from home) drives from home to a customer site in Leeds (50 miles from home) and back. Business miles = (50 − 12) x 2 = 76 miles. They have claimed fewer than 10,000 business miles this tax year. Reimbursement = 76 x £0.55 = **£41.80** .

An employee has already claimed 9,950 business miles in the 2026/27 tax year and makes a 120-mile business journey. The first 50 miles are paid at 55p and the remaining 70 at 25p: (50 x £0.55) + (70 x £0.25) = £27.50 + £17.50 = **£45.00** .

## **Example 14.5 — Berlin trip (Band B), currency conversion**

An employee travels to Berlin for 3 nights with Director pre-approval and a travel-risk check. The hotel costs €210 per night on the corporate card; the card statement shows £181.50 per night including fees, which is within the £200 Band B limit, so £544.50 is reimbursed for 3 nights. A taxi costing €30 was paid in cash; Finance's published rate for that month is 1.16 euros per £1, so the claim is €30 / 1.16 = **£25.86** . Because the total claim exceeds £250, it needs line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.6 — client dinner**

A dinner for 4 people (2 client attendees and 2 Northstar employees) costs £296.00 including drinks, which is £74.00 per head. This is above the £60 per head limit by 23%, so the Head of Department (who must pre-approve all client entertainment) may approve the excess as an exception up to 25% above the limit. If the bill had been £320.00 (£80.00 per head, 33% above the limit), Director approval would be required for the excess. Neither amount exceeds £100 per head, so no gifts and hospitality register entry is required.

- An expense incurred on Wednesday 3 March 2027 and submitted on Thursday 15 April 2027 is 43 calendar days old: a late claim needing a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- The same expense submitted on Saturday 5 June 2027 would be 94 calendar days old and would not be reimbursed unless the Finance Director approved an exception.

- A claim fully approved on 9 March 2027 is paid on Thursday 25 March 2027. A claim fully approved on 12 March 2027 is paid in the April payroll; because 25 April 2027 is a Sunday, it is paid on Friday 23 April 2027.

expected_output: Notice counts working days between submission and the first day of leave, excluding both: 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 February = 9 working days. Leave of more than 1 and up to 5 days needs 10 working days, so this is short notice; the manager may still approve at their discretion. Starting on Tuesday 16 February would have given 10.

input: I'm full-time and took 5 days of annual leave in a 4-week period. How many office days do I need in that period? And what if I worked 3 days a week?
expected_output: Absence reduces the requirement proportionally, rounded up to a whole day: 8 x (15 available / 20 normal working days) = 6 days. For a part-time 3-day week the normal requirement is 8 x 3/5 = 4.8, rounded up to 5 days per rolling 4-week period.
context: For a full-time employee with 5 days of annual leave in a 4-week period of 20 working days: 8 x 15 / 20 = 6 days.
For a 3-day week: 8 x 3 / 5 = 4.8, rounded up to 5 days per rolling 4-week period.

Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Office attendance standard > 4.3 Part-time employees and absence

The requirement is pro-rated and rounded **up** to the nearest whole day:

- **Part-time:** required days = 8 x (contracted working days per week / 5). For a 3-day week: 8 x 3 / 5 = 4.8, rounded up to **5 days** per rolling 4-week period.

- **Annual leave, sickness, bank holidays and other approved absence:** required days = (normal requirement) x (available working days in the period / normal working days in the period). For a full-time employee with 5 days of annual leave in a 4-week period of 20 working days: 8 x 15 / 20 = **6 days** .

input: Northstar is dismissing a G2 engineer with 9 complete years of service. How much notice must they give?
expected_output: Northstar must give the greater of contractual notice (1 month for G1–G3 after probation) and statutory notice (1 week per complete year of service from 2 years, up to 12 weeks). 9 years = 9 weeks, which is longer than 1 month, so 9 weeks' notice is required. If the employee resigned, they would only need to give 1 month.

input: An employee aged 35 with 6 full years' service (all after age 22) and weekly pay of £900 is made redundant in November 2026. What is the statutory redundancy pay?
expected_output: Statutory redundancy pay requires 2+ years' service. For years aged 22–40, it is one week's pay per full year: 6 weeks. Weekly pay is capped at £751 for redundancies on or after 6 April 2026, so 6 x £751 = £4,506. Any enhanced terms are discretionary and not guaranteed.
context: For redundancies on or after 6 April 2026, weekly pay is capped at £751 and the maximum statutory redundancy payment is £22,530.
one week's pay for each full year aged 22 to 40
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.2 Redundancy

A redundancy situation arises where Northstar needs fewer employees to do work of a particular kind, or work ceases at a location. Northstar will consult individually with affected employees, use fair and objective selection criteria, consider ways to avoid redundancy and offer suitable alternative employment where available. Where it proposes 20 or more redundancies at one establishment within 90 days, Northstar will also carry out collective consultation in line with the statutory minimum periods and notify the Secretary of State.

### **Statutory redundancy pay**

Employees with at least 2 years' continuous service are entitled to statutory redundancy pay: half a week's pay for each full year of service under age 22; one week's pay for each full year aged 22 to 40; and one and a half weeks' pay for each full year aged 41 or over. Service is capped at 20 years. For redundancies on or after 6 April 2026, weekly pay is capped at £751 and the maximum statutory redundancy payment is £22,530. Any enhanced redundancy terms are discretionary and will be confirmed in writing at the time; none are guaranteed by this handbook.

Employees under notice of redundancy with at least 2 years' service may take reasonable paid time off to look for work or arrange training.

input: A full-time employee joins on 16 September 2027. How much annual leave do they get for 2027?
expected_output: Calendar days 16 September–31 December 2027 inclusive = 107. 27 x 107 / 365 = 7.915, rounded up to 8.0 days, plus the bank holidays on 27 and 28 December. Three days must be kept for the 29–31 December 2027 shutdown.

3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

- **Full-time joiner, 1 March 2027:** 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.636, rounded up to **23.0 days** , plus 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027.

- **Part-time joiner, 1 July 2027, 22.5 hours Monday to Wednesday:** 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397, rounded up to **79.5 hours** . Bank holidays on working days (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) = 22.5 hours. Bookable annual leave = **57.0 hours** .

expected_output: Grades G4 and G5 give 2 months' contractual notice after probation.

retrieval_context:

minimum| |After probation, grades G4 and G5|2 months|The greater of 2 months and the statutory
minimum| |After probation, grades G6 and G7|3 months|The greater of 3 months and the statutory
minimum| ## **Statutory minimum notice** An employee with more than 1 month's service must give at least 1 week's notice. An employer must give at least 1 week's notice to an employee with between 1 month and 2 years' service, then 1 week for each complete year of service from 2 years, up to a maximum of 12 weeks after 12 years. A contract can give more than these minimums but never less. Notice periods in Table 22.4 are illustrative Northstar contractual terms; the individual employment contract prevails. **Example.** Northstar gives notice to a G2 engineer with 9 complete years of service. If the same engineer resigns, they need give only their contractual notice of 1 month.
