input: I'm 0.6 FTE. How much leave can I carry over and by when must I use it?
expected_output: The handbook sets the standard carryover of 5 days pro-rated by FTE, used by 31 March; the Leave and Absence Standard specifies the part-time limit as 37.5 hours x FTE, so 37.5 x 0.6 = 22.5 hours.
context: Carried-over leave must be taken by 31 March of the next leave year.
an employee at 0.6 FTE may carry over up to 37.5 x 0.6 = 22.5 hours
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.11 Carrying over unused leave ## **Standard carryover rule** Up to **5 days** (37.5 hours for a full-time employee; pro-rated for part-time employees by FTE) of unused annual leave may be carried over into the next leave year without approval. Carried-over leave must be taken by **31 March** of the next leave year. Carried-over leave not taken by 31 March is lost, unless one of the exceptions below applies. **Table 6.11 — Carryover exceptions** |**Situation**|**Rule**|**Approval and deadline**| |---|---|---| |Employee could not take leave
because of sickness absence|Untaken leave up to 4 weeks (20 days full-time,
pro-rated) may be carried over, in addition to
the standard 5 days.|Automatic on evidence of the sickness
absence. Must be taken within 18
months of the end of the leave year in
which it accrued.| |Employee was on maternity,
adoption, shared parental, neonatal
care or other family-related leave|All untaken annual leave for the leave year is
carried over.|Automatic. Must be taken within 12
months of the return-to-work date.| |Exceptional business reasons
(employee asked by the company to
defer leave)|A further 5 days may be carried over (up to 10
days in total).|Request by 30 November in PeopleHub,
approved by the Director of People
Operations. Must be taken by 30 June of
the next leave year.| Carryover beyond these limits is not available. An approved carryover exception is not a precedent for future years.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.8 Carryover **Table 3.8 — Carryover rules** |**Type**|**Maximum**|**Deadline to use**|**Approval**| |---|---|---|---| |Standard|5 days (37.5 hours x FTE)|31 March of the next leave
year|None| |Sickness prevented leave|Up to 4 weeks (20 days x
FTE), in addition to
standard|18 months after the end of
the leave year in which it
accrued|Automatic, with absence
records| |Family-related leave prevented leave|All untaken leave for the
year|12 months after the
return-to-work date|Automatic| |Exceptional business reasons|A further 5 days (10 days
total)|30 June of the next leave year|Director of People
Operations; request by 30
November| ## **Worked examples 3.8 — carryover** - **Standard:** a full-time employee has 27 days in 2027 and has taken 20 days by 31 December 2027 (including the 3 shutdown days). Unused = 7 days. They carry over **5 days** , which must be taken by 31 March 2028, and **2 days are lost** unless an exception is approved. - **Part-time limit:** an employee at 0.6 FTE may carry over up to 37.5 x 0.6 = **22.5 hours** . - **Sickness:** a full-time employee was on sick leave from September to December 2027 and has 15 unused days. They carry over 5 standard days (use by 31 March 2028) and the remaining 10 days under the sickness rule (use by 30 June 2029, 18 months after 31 December 2027). - **2026 into 2027:** a full-time employee with a 2026 transitional entitlement of 25.5 days took 22 days in 2026. Unused = 3.5 days, which is within the 5-day limit, so all **3.5 days** carry over and must be taken by 31 March 2027.

expected_output: Both the handbook and the Expenses Policy require leavers to submit all claims within 10 working days after the leaving date; claims received after that are not paid. The corporate card is cancelled on the last working day.

information; drafting and summarising documents; using CodePilot Enterprise on Northstar-owned source

input: Does a business trip to a customer in Dublin count towards my 10 Work From Abroad days?
expected_output: The Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard says travel abroad at Northstar's request for customer or company work is a business trip under NDS-FIN-EXP-003 and does not count towards the 10 days. It needs Director pre-approval and a travel-risk check under the Expenses Policy.
context: Travel abroad at Northstar's request for customer or company work is a business trip under NDS-FIN-EXP-003 and does not count towards the 10 days.
Working from abroad outside a business trip is covered by NDS-HR-HFW-005 section 7, not this policy.
retrieval_context:
Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01) 7 Working from outside the UK > 7.1 Rules **Table 7.1 — Work From Abroad rules** |**Rule**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Maximum|**10 working days**in any rolling 12-month period. Any working day on which any work is
performed abroad counts as a full day.| |Request|PeopleHub Work From Abroad request at least**4 weeks**before travel.| |Approvals|Line manager, People Operations (tax, social security and immigration screening) and IT
Security (destination and data check). All three are required.| |Eligibility|Employees who have completed probation and are not serving notice.| |Destinations|Not permitted to destinations on the IT Security restricted-destination list.| |Data|Public, Internal and Confidential information may be accessed through Northstar Secure
Connect.**Restricted**information must not be accessed unless the CISO has approved it in
writing and the customer contract permits access from outside the UK.| |Availability|The employee must be available for UK core hours (10:00 to 16:00 UK time).| |Exceptions|More than 10 days requires Director of People Operations approval and external tax and
immigration advice; no exception may exceed**20 working days**in a rolling 12-month
period.| |Business trips|Travel abroad at Northstar's request for customer or company work is a business trip under
NDS-FIN-EXP-003 and does not count towards the 10 days.|

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 International travel and currency conversion

- International trips require Director pre-approval and a Travel desk travel-risk check before booking. Trips to destinations rated high risk also need CISO approval for any devices taken (a clean travel laptop may be issued).

- Working from abroad outside a business trip is covered by NDS-HR-HFW-005 section 7, not this policy.

- **Currency conversion:** claim in pounds sterling. For card payments (corporate or personal), use the sterling amount on the card statement, including any foreign transaction fee, and attach the statement line. For cash payments, use Finance's published monthly exchange rate for the month in which the expense was incurred (published on the intranet as foreign currency units per £1). Sterling amount = foreign amount / published rate, rounded to the nearest penny.

- Limits in Table 4.8 are applied to the sterling amount.

input: Does Northstar enhance Shared Parental Pay?
expected_output: Both the handbook and the Leave and Absence Standard state that Northstar pays ShPP only (£194.32 or 90% of AWE if lower) with no company enhancement, unlike maternity and adoption pay.
context: Northstar pays ShPP only; there is no company enhancement for shared parental pay.
No company enhancement.
retrieval_context:

8 Family-related leave > 8.4 Shared parental leave and pay

Eligible parents can share up to **50 weeks** of leave and up to **37 weeks** of pay by ending maternity or adoption leave early. Eligibility depends on both parents: the employee must meet the continuity of employment test (normally 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the EWC or by the week of matching, and still employed in the first week of shared parental leave), and the other parent must meet the employment and earnings test. The employee must give at least **8 weeks' written notice** of leave dates. Requests for discontinuous blocks may be refused; the employee may then take the leave as one continuous block. Northstar pays ShPP only; there is no company enhancement for shared parental pay.

input: Is my home broadband reimbursable as part of hybrid working?
expected_output: The Hybrid Standard and the Expenses Policy both state broadband and utilities are not reimbursed; the home office allowance is up to £300 once per 3 years after probation for desks, chairs or ergonomic items.

Broadband, utilities and personal mobile contracts are not reimbursable.

input: What are the deadlines in the flexible-working process?
expected_output: The handbook and the Hybrid Standard set: acknowledgement within 5 working days; a meeting within 4 weeks; whole process including appeal within 2 months unless the employee agrees an extension; appeal within 10 working days of the decision, heard by a more senior manager. Refusal only after consultation for a statutory business reason; trials up to 3 months.
context: The whole process, including any appeal, must be completed within 2 months of the date the request was received, unless the employee agrees to extend it.
The line manager acknowledges the request within 5 working days.
retrieval_context:
Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01) 5 Formal flexible-working requests > 5.2 Procedure **Table 5.2 — Flexible-working procedure and deadlines** |**Step**|**Action**|**Deadline**| |---|---|---| |1|Employee submits the PeopleHub "Statutory flexible working
request" form, stating it is a statutory request, the date, the
pattern requested and proposed start date, and any previous
request and its date.|—| |2|Line manager acknowledges the request.|Within 5 working days of receipt| |3|Line manager meets the employee to discuss the request and
possible alternatives. The employee may be accompanied by a
colleague or trade union representative.|Within 4 weeks of receipt| |4|Written decision: approve, approve with modifications or a trial, or
refuse with the statutory reasons explained.|In time to allow any appeal within the 2-month
period| |5|Employee may appeal in writing.|Within 10 working days of the decision| |6|Appeal heard by a more senior manager not involved in the original
decision; written appeal outcome.|Within the 2-month period, unless the employee
agrees an extension| The whole process, including any appeal, must be completed within **2 months** of the date the request was received, unless the employee agrees to extend it. If the employee fails to attend two meetings without good reason, the request may be treated as withdrawn, and the employee is told this in writing.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.6 Formal flexible-working requests

All employees can make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment, and can make up to **2 statutory requests in any 12-month period** . A request can cover hours, start and finish times, working days, or place of work.

## **Flexible working — process and deadlines**

1. Submit a written request in PeopleHub stating that it is a statutory request for flexible working, the date of the request, the working pattern requested and the proposed start date, and whether and when any earlier request was made. 2. The line manager acknowledges the request within **5 working days** . 3. The line manager meets the employee to discuss the request within **4 weeks** of receiving it. A request cannot be refused without first consulting the employee. 4. A written decision is issued, and any appeal concluded, within **2 months** of the date of the request, unless the employee agrees to an extension. 5. A refusal must give one or more of the statutory business reasons and explain why it applies. 6. The employee may appeal within **10 working days** of the decision. The appeal is heard by a different, more senior manager.

The statutory business reasons for refusing a request are: the burden of additional costs; inability to reorganise work among existing staff; inability to recruit additional staff; a detrimental effect on quality; a detrimental effect on performance; a detrimental effect on ability to meet customer demand; insufficient work during the periods the employee proposes to work; and planned structural changes. Managers may agree a **trial period of up to 3 months** before confirming a permanent change.

input: If a search result from the archived Leave Policy conflicts with the Leave and Absence Standard, which should I follow?
expected_output: The handbook precedence rule says a superseded or archived document never takes precedence over a current document. The Leave and Absence Standard supersedes NDS-HR-LV-006 from 1 October 2026, and the archived document itself says not to use it for current decisions. Use it only for dates before 1 October 2026 or where the transitional rules point to it.
context: A superseded or archived document never takes precedence over a current document.
Do not use it to answer questions about current entitlements
retrieval_context:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
1 Introduction and document governance > 1.5 Policy hierarchy and conflict resolution

If two sources appear to conflict, apply the following order of precedence, subject always to mandatory law:

1. Applicable mandatory law.

2. The employee's applicable employment contract or written contractual variation.

3. The current, topic-specific approved policy or standard (for example, the Leave and Absence Standard NDS-HR-LAS-002).

4. This current Employee Handbook summary.

5. Non-binding manager guidance.

A superseded or archived document never takes precedence over a current document. Archived documents are retained only to show what applied during their effective period. When a question concerns a past date, use the document whose effective period covers that date; when it concerns a current or future date, use the current document.

If an employee or manager identifies a genuine conflict between current documents, they should apply the higher-ranked source and report the conflict to people@northstar.example so that the documents can be corrected.

additional_metadata.source_sections: NDS-HR-HB-001 section 1.5; NDS-HR-LV-006 section Superseded notice

input: The induction deck says someone starting full-time on 1 March 2027 can book 9 days by 1 June. Does the Leave and Absence Standard agree?
expected_output: Both agree. The Leave and Absence Standard section 3.2 gives the same worked example: 3 complete months by 1 June, accrued 6.75 days rounded up to 7.0, plus up to 2 additional days with line manager approval = 9.0 days. Leave of more than 5 consecutive working days in probation also needs Head of Department approval. The Standard is authoritative; the deck is a summary.
context: Bookable: 7.0 + 2 = 9.0 days
With line manager approval they may book up to 7.0 + 2 = 9.0 days
retrieval_context:

Slide 4

## Booking leave while you're in probation

Full-time: 27 days a year plus 8 bank holidays, pro-rated in your first year
In probation you can book leave you have accrued, plus up to 2 more days with your manager's approval
Request in PeopleHub; 10 working days' notice for 2 to 5 days
Keep 3 days for the shutdown: 29 to 31 December
Worked example
You start full-time on 1 March 2027.
On 1 June you have 3 complete months.
Accrued: 27 × 3 ÷ 12 = 6.75, rounded up to 7.0 days
Bookable: 7.0 + 2 = 9.0 days
Your 2027 entitlement is 23.0 days (27 × 306 ÷ 365, rounded up to the nearest half day).

Speaker notes: Leave of more than 5 consecutive working days during probation also needs Head of Department approval. Leave is not approved until PeopleHub shows Approved, so do not book non-refundable travel before then.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.2 Accrual and booking

Leave accrues at one-twelfth of the annual entitlement per complete calendar month. After probation, the full annual entitlement may be booked in advance. During probation, the bookable amount is accrued leave (rounded up to the nearest 0.5 day) plus up to 2 additional days with line manager approval.

### **Booking during probation**

A full-time employee starts on 1 March 2027. On 1 June 2027 they have 3 complete months of service. Accrued leave = 27 x 3 / 12 = 6.75 days, rounded up to 7.0 days. With line manager approval they may book up to 7.0 + 2 = **9.0 days** for leave starting on or around that date. Any period of more than 5 consecutive working days also needs Head of Department approval.

input: If a training slide and the policy document say different things, which should I follow?
expected_output: Each deck states it is a summary and that where it differs from a policy document, the policy document prevails. The handbook precedence order puts mandatory law, the contract, the topic-specific standard and the handbook above non-binding guidance.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
1 Introduction and document governance > 1.5 Policy hierarchy and conflict resolution

If two sources appear to conflict, apply the following order of precedence, subject always to mandatory law:

1. Applicable mandatory law.

2. The employee's applicable employment contract or written contractual variation.

3. The current, topic-specific approved policy or standard (for example, the Leave and Absence Standard NDS-HR-LAS-002).

4. This current Employee Handbook summary.

5. Non-binding manager guidance.

A superseded or archived document never takes precedence over a current document. Archived documents are retained only to show what applied during their effective period. When a question concerns a past date, use the document whose effective period covers that date; when it concerns a current or future date, use the current document.

If an employee or manager identifies a genuine conflict between current documents, they should apply the higher-ranked source and report the conflict to people@northstar.example so that the documents can be corrected.

input: Per the manager briefing, how much company sick pay does an employee with 3 years' service get?
expected_output: Employees with 2 to under 5 years' service get 8 weeks at full pay followed by 8 weeks at half pay in any rolling 12-month period, inclusive of SSP (briefing chart and notes; handbook Table 7.5 is authoritative).
context: 2 to under 5 years, 8 weeks full then 8 weeks half
2 years or more but less than 5 years | 8 weeks | 8 weeks
retrieval_context:
What changes on 1 October 2026: Manager Briefing (NDS-HR-PRES-011 v1.0, summary deck, current, effective 2026-10-01)
Slide 6

## Sickness: call by 09:30, SSP from day one

Employees call (phone or Teams) by 09:30 on day one; messages alone are not enough
Self-certify up to 7 calendar days; fit note after that
Since 6 April 2026, SSP is paid from the first day: £123.25 a week or 80% of earnings, whichever is lower
Company sick pay is inclusive of SSP and starts after probation
Pregnancy-related absence never counts towards triggers

Speaker notes: Company sick pay in any rolling 12 months: during probation SSP only; probation completed and under 2 years, 4 weeks full pay then 4 weeks half pay; 2 to under 5 years, 8 weeks full then 8 weeks half; 5 years or more, 13 weeks full then 13 weeks half. Attendance triggers: 3 separate absences or 8 working days in a rolling 12 months starts a supportive Stage 0 review. Disability-related absence is recorded separately and triggers may be adjusted.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.5 Company sick pay

Company sick pay is a contractual enhancement for employees whose contract incorporates the company sick pay scheme (all permanent and fixed-term employment contracts issued from 1 January 2025). It is paid **inclusive of SSP** : SSP forms part of, and is not paid in addition to, company sick pay.

**Table 7.5 — Company sick pay entitlement in any rolling 12-month period**

|**Continuous service on the first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Then half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed and less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more but less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

- The rolling 12-month period is the 12 months ending on the day before the first day of the current absence. Company sick pay already paid in that period is deducted from the entitlement.

- "Half pay" is half of basic pay; where half pay would be less than SSP, SSP is paid instead. After company sick pay is exhausted, SSP continues if the statutory conditions are met.

- Weeks are calculated by reference to the employee's normal working days (for example, one week for a 3-day-per-week employee is 3 working days).

- Company sick pay is conditional on following the reporting procedure in section 7.1 and providing the evidence in section 7.3. If the employee does not follow these steps without a good reason, company sick pay may be withheld for the affected days. Statutory Sick Pay is still paid where the statutory conditions are met.

- Contractors and agency workers are not eligible for company sick pay.

**Example.** An employee with 3 years' continuous service has received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months. They are now absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay entitlement = 8 − 5 = 3 weeks. They

therefore receive 3 weeks at full pay followed by 3 weeks at half pay (they have 8 weeks of half-pay entitlement available).

What changes on 1 October 2026: Manager Briefing (NDS-HR-PRES-011 v1.0, summary deck, current, effective 2026-10-01)
Slide 6

## Sickness: call by 09:30, SSP from day one

Employees call (phone or Teams) by 09:30 on day one; messages alone are not enough
Self-certify up to 7 calendar days; fit note after that
Since 6 April 2026, SSP is paid from the first day: £123.25 a week or 80% of earnings, whichever is lower
Company sick pay is inclusive of SSP and starts after probation
Pregnancy-related absence never counts towards triggers

Speaker notes: Company sick pay in any rolling 12 months: during probation SSP only; probation completed and under 2 years, 4 weeks full pay then 4 weeks half pay; 2 to under 5 years, 8 weeks full then 8 weeks half; 5 years or more, 13 weeks full then 13 weeks half. Attendance triggers: 3 separate absences or 8 working days in a rolling 12 months starts a supportive Stage 0 review. Disability-related absence is recorded separately and triggers may be adjusted.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.5 Company sick pay

Company sick pay is a contractual enhancement for employees whose contract incorporates the company sick pay scheme (all permanent and fixed-term employment contracts issued from 1 January 2025). It is paid **inclusive of SSP** : SSP forms part of, and is not paid in addition to, company sick pay.

**Table 7.5 — Company sick pay entitlement in any rolling 12-month period**

|**Continuous service on the first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Then half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed and less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more but less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

- The rolling 12-month period is the 12 months ending on the day before the first day of the current absence. Company sick pay already paid in that period is deducted from the entitlement.

- "Half pay" is half of basic pay; where half pay would be less than SSP, SSP is paid instead. After company sick pay is exhausted, SSP continues if the statutory conditions are met.

- Weeks are calculated by reference to the employee's normal working days (for example, one week for a 3-day-per-week employee is 3 working days).

- Company sick pay is conditional on following the reporting procedure in section 7.1 and providing the evidence in section 7.3. If the employee does not follow these steps without a good reason, company sick pay may be withheld for the affected days. Statutory Sick Pay is still paid where the statutory conditions are met.

- Contractors and agency workers are not eligible for company sick pay.

**Example.** An employee with 3 years' continuous service has received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months. They are now absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay entitlement = 8 − 5 = 3 weeks. They

therefore receive 3 weeks at full pay followed by 3 weeks at half pay (they have 8 weeks of half-pay entitlement available).
